headline: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation

key_points: Five LLMs (GPT‑5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, BioGPT) were benchmarked on five heterogeneous KGs.
General‑purpose models outperformed domain‑specific models on complex multi‑hop queries.
Graph‑grounded (KG‑aware) prompting lowered hallucination rates for all models.
Performance drops as query complexity rises, highlighting limits of current LLM reasoning.
Guidance offered for LLM‑KG integration strategies and hybrid neurosymbolic architectures.
why_it_matters: Understanding how LLMs interact with structured knowledge is crucial for reliable biomedical and cognitive applications, such as personalized medicine and explainable AI, where factual accuracy and reduced hallucination are essential.

headline: Show HN: Stroq – a local audit of what your coding agent did and why

Apache‑2.0 licensed and installable via npm
why_it_matters: As AI coding assistants gain access to local files and secrets, developers need a way to ensure those agents don’t unintentionally leak credentials or execute harmful commands. Stroq gives transparent, auditable control without sacrificing privacy.

Runs agent loops outside the sandbox, cutting idle VM costs
Deployable via Docker, Kubernetes, VM, or Rivet Cloud on AWS/GCP

headline: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates

key_points: Introduces a scalable template augmentation method to generate multilingual refusal and benign data.
Releases MSafeTemp, a validated corpus spanning 60 languages for safety alignment and evaluation.
Demonstrates that models safe in English can be vulnerable in other languages and cultures.
Shows that multilingual safety training via templates boosts safety performance beyond English.
why_it_matters: Safety alignment has been English‑centric, leaving low‑resource languages exposed to harmful outputs. Providing a large, culturally diverse dataset enables researchers to evaluate and improve safety across languages, reducing risks for under‑represented users.

headline: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
tldr: Drex introduces four open-source decision models that output probability distributions over options without autoregressive decoding, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and low latency.
key_points: Four models released (8B, 9B, 35B active 3B, 27B) with open-source code
Uses supervised fine-tuning plus RLAF and consistency losses for robustness
Achieves 67.52 on Decision Index 0.4.1, beating prior decision models
Fast inference: 183 ms per request vs. seconds for comparable models
Supports multimodal inputs (text and images) in the Max variant
why_it_matters: Decision models provide consistent, low-latency predictions for classification‑type tasks, addressing key limitations of large autoregressive LLMs such as output variability and high compute cost, and the open release enables broader research and deployment.

headline: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
tldr: Introduces Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD) and VA-TDM framework to boost quality of few-step diffusion models, achieving state‑of‑the‑art results in 4‑step text‑to‑image and text‑to‑video generation.
key_points: VAD uses a learned critic to compare teacher and student velocity fields, turning their disagreement into training feedback.
VA‑TDM provides trajectory distribution matching with transition‑aware online velocity learning for intermediate steps.
Achieves SOTA four‑step performance on text‑to‑image and text‑to‑video tasks, scaling up to a 33B MiniMax‑H3 model.
Unifies score distillation, Fisher‑based matching, and moment matching, explaining existing heuristic updates.
why_it_matters: Improving few‑step diffusion generation reduces compute and latency while preserving quality, making high‑fidelity AI image and video creation more practical for real‑time and resource‑constrained applications.

headline: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
tldr: NPCBench introduces a 4,777-item benchmark with a 100‑patient care‑pathway cohort to evaluate AI models on multimodal, longitudinal reasoning in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, revealing a large gap between task‑level and care‑pathway performance.
key_points: Benchmarks 4,777 component/consultation items plus 100‑patient CarePath cohort (417 scored tasks).
Evaluates models on integrated diagnostic and care decisions across patient trajectories.
Across 30 models, only up to 23% achieve strict CarePath success despite strong individual task scores.
Includes paired controls and physician calibration to test evidence grounding and longitudinal revision.
Provides an apprenticeship‑style testbed for temporally coherent oncology AI reasoning.
why_it_matters: Current medical AI benchmarks focus on isolated questions, missing how models handle real‑world, multimodal clinical workflows. NPCBench pushes evaluation toward realistic care pathways, highlighting gaps that must be closed before AI can safely assist oncologists in longitudinal patient management.

Reduces prediction error versus autoregressive decoding on 2D/3D tasks
Achieves ~25× faster generation for 3D motion forecasting
Improves downstream task success to 70.2% vs 62.6% baseline
why_it_matters: Faster, more accurate visual planning enables real‑time decision making for robotics and autonomous systems, lowering computational costs while boosting performance on complex spatial tasks.

headline: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
tldr: D3D introduces a diffusion-based drafter that removes inter-round dependencies, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding and achieving up to 7.5× speedup on large language models.
key_points: Standalone diffusion drafter eliminates need for target-model hidden states during drafting.
Combines blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision for long accepted prefixes.
Layer pruning retains >99% acceptance length while reducing computational cost.
Achieves 5–7.5× decoding speedup on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B compared to prior methods.
why_it_matters: Faster decoding reduces inference latency and cost for large language models, making real-time applications more feasible and improving efficiency of speculative decoding techniques.

headline: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
tldr: A new method, Harness‑S, uses specialized sibling harnesses to rescue failures during training and transfers those capabilities into a single policy that works under the original harness.
key_points: Directional Harness Evolution creates a fixed pool of specialized sibling harnesses.
Complementary Harness Rescue Training invokes the pool only when the base harness fails.
An Adaptive Harness Router selects top‑k harnesses using behavior profiles and LLM voting.
Experiments on AppWorld, SWE‑Gym, and DBBench show substantial gains over policy‑only training.
why_it_matters: The approach demonstrates a scalable way to improve agent robustness by leveraging multiple corrective environments, reducing the need for a universally superior harness and enabling better generalization of learned policies.

headline: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand

key_points: Random sampling can approximate full benchmark scores but has a long-tailed error distribution.
BestRand reduces the high-error tail and overall estimation error while maintaining low cost.
Validated on 70+ text, multimodal, and agent benchmarks, achieving up to 21.8% lower OOD error.
Requires only 51.3% of the construction cost compared to competitive methods.
Code and data are publicly released on GitHub.
why_it_matters: Efficient and reliable benchmark compression enables faster evaluation of many AI models, accelerating research cycles and reducing computational expenses, especially as the number of foundation models grows.

headline: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation

Jointly improving teacher capability and data coverage eliminates OOD forgetting.
Geometry-based patching and base-preserving replay boost OOD performance while preserving IND results.
why_it_matters: Understanding and fixing the OOD generalization gap in distillation methods is crucial for reliably transferring capabilities from large teacher models to smaller or specialized models, impacting the efficiency and safety of AI deployment.

headline: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens

Explicit tokens are retained only for tool interactions and final answers.
Improves accuracy by up to 8.8 points on benchmark tasks.
Reduces model forward passes by up to 6.8×.
Enhances tool-use quality in single- and multi-tool scenarios.

headline: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding

Demonstrated on 8B, 27B, and 125B models across dialogue, coding, math, and agentic tasks.
why_it_matters: Increasing the efficiency of large language model inference reduces latency and compute costs, making high‑performance models more practical for real‑time applications and broader deployment.

headline: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference

Introduces the SIMPLE law, a four‑parameter model separating prefill and decode costs, achieving R² = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE across 13 dense LLMs.
Shows prefill energy grows quadratically with hidden dimension and that GQA reduces per‑token energy up to 3× versus standard MHA.
Finds agentic serving increases energy per request by 13×, while prefix caching cuts prefill cost by 93% but leaves KV‑cache cost largely unchanged.
why_it_matters: Understanding and accurately predicting the energy cost of LLM inference enables more efficient model deployment, informs hardware and architecture choices, and helps balance performance with sustainability as LLMs scale.

tldr: Multi-turn RL boosts long‑horizon LLM agents but only when interaction budgets are generous; BudgetMix RL varies budgets during training to achieve stable performance.
key_points: Performance gains depend heavily on turn budget (K, T).
RL mainly helps error recovery and long‑horizon resilience, not single‑step decisions.
BudgetMix RL varies interaction budgets during training for robustness.
Experiments show consistent results across diverse execution settings.
why_it_matters: Understanding budget sensitivity guides safer deployment of RL‑enhanced LLM agents and informs training strategies that remain effective under real‑world resource constraints.

headline: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research

key_points: 56 real-world physics tasks created by 42 physicists covering nine domains
Agents must review literature, plan research, conduct experiments, and write manuscripts
Deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics assess correctness and publishability
22 models in 26 configurations failed to pass more than 46 of 168 rollouts
Weaknesses stem from insufficient rigorous reasoning and expert intuition
why_it_matters: The benchmark highlights current AI agents' inability to conduct end-to-end scientific research, guiding future development toward more robust reasoning and domain expertise needed for real scientific discovery.

headline: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling

Unified pipeline adds scene‑consistent segmentation, quality filtering, camera pose estimation, and event‑based captions
Temporally stable camera trajectories and event‑aligned captions improve long‑horizon controllability
Benchmark experiments show models trained on GameVerse achieve substantially longer coherent rollouts
why_it_matters: Current interactive world models falter after ~1 minute due to a lack of long‑horizon training data; GameVerse provides the scale and annotation quality needed to push temporal coherence forward, enabling more realistic and controllable virtual environments.

headline: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games

why_it_matters: Shows a practical way to generalize live video commentary across games without retraining on each title, advancing multimodal LLMs toward broader, real‑time applications.

headline: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL

key_points: Uses reward traces from ongoing training to adaptively weight emotional cues.
Introduces Reflective Reward Gating and RewardMemory for instance‑level calibration.
Shows consistent gains on HunyuanVideo 1.5 and transfers to SD 3.5 and FLUX.
Mitigates reward hacking and the need for extensive RLHF scaling.
why_it_matters: Accurate emotional expression in generated video is hard to quantify; EmoReward offers a scalable way to align rewards with subjective aesthetics, advancing the quality and reliability of AI‑driven video creation.

Outperforms previous methods on multiple composed image retrieval benchmarks.
why_it_matters: Improves the ability of multimodal LLMs to understand and apply textual modifications to images, advancing retrieval systems that combine visual and textual cues.

headline: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit

Proposes turn-level credit assignment using silence-completed prefix scoring.
Introduces turn-mean policy optimization to weight response and waiting decisions equally.
Demonstrates superior performance over prior RL methods in extensive experiments.
why_it_matters: Better credit assignment at the turn level enables more accurate and efficient streaming video models, leading to more responsive AI systems for real-time video analysis and interaction.

headline: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
tldr: NEO-VLA introduces an encoder-free vision-language-action framework that jointly processes visual and language tokens, showing that native architectures outperform traditional encoder-based models for embodied manipulation tasks.
key_points: NEO-VLA tokenizes images with lightweight patch convolutions and integrates them with language throughout the backbone.
Native architectures outperform encoder-based counterparts, especially for action-critical visual signals that appear early in the network.
Full fine-tuning narrows but does not eliminate the performance gap, and scaling alone cannot recover it.
The approach yields stronger, more robust control across diverse manipulation settings and distribution shifts.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates that allowing action policies to access visual representations at multiple depths improves embodied AI performance, challenging the prevailing encoder-first paradigm and guiding future model design for robotics and interactive systems.
